title: Load-controlled Hertz contact: contact radius and indentation vs closed form (case pool FEM-HERTZ-CONTACT)

gates.reference: a = (3 P R / (4 E*))^(1/3), E* = E/(1-nu^2) (rigid indenter)
the indentation error saturates at a mesh-independent plateau; refinement must not move it by more than 0.5 pp
gates.note: a stricter 'monotone decrease' gate was drafted first and FAILED by 1.4e-3 pp: the error plateaus at -1.01% instead of tending to zero, i.e. the residual is a systematic model offset, not discretisation noise

gates.quantity: max |residual| of the fitted law err(D) = e_inf + c/D over the depth ladder (pp)
gates.reference: a fixed outer boundary at depth D perturbs the half-space compliance as O(1/D); five depths 24a..192a must collapse onto that law

gates.quantity: max |measured - predicted| indentation error at D = 144a, 192a when the 1/D law is fitted only on D = 24a, 48a, 96a (pp)
|e_inf| = indentation error extrapolated to an unbounded domain (%)
gates.reference: delta = a^2 / R with the truncation term removed
gates.note: this is the honest accuracy statement of the accepted model: at D = 96a the measured |error| is ~1.0%, of which the modelled truncation term accounts for ~0.63 pp; the remainder is mesh/far-field independent

gates.reference: if refinement moves the residual, the plateau is discretisation; if it does not, it is a fixed model offset
the 1/D term must be domain size, not far-field meshing

limitations: Rigid parabolic indenter on an elastic half-space: the FE model is the Hertz reduction itself, so this grades the discretisation and the contact algorithm, not a deformable-body generalisation.

The contact radius is estimated from the computed pressure field (linear zero crossing between the last two active nodes); at a/R = 0.02 the patch edge falls between coarse nodes and the estimator degrades -- recorded as probe_low_load, deliberately outside the gates.
Depth truncation is a modelling error, not a discretisation error: it is quantified by the truncation ladder rather than eliminated.
No friction; no material or geometric nonlinearity (linear elasticity, small strain).
